_doc: The Green/Yellow/Red rules of SPEC.md section 5.7, as data.
Every rule that can move a score lives here with the reason it gives, so
a rating can be explained from its inputs and no number that decides one
is buried in code. A rule has a cap (the most a file it fires on can
score) and/or a penalty (points off). The score is 100 minus every
penalty, held under the lowest cap that fired.
The loss policy agreed for Milestone 5: RED when the header cluster or
half or more of the clusters are lost; YELLOW for smaller losses; GREEN
only with nothing lost. A file with no structural validator can still be
GREEN on evidence - intact metadata, no lost cluster - and says so.

trimmed.why: The device reports TRIM and every cluster reads as zero: the controller has discarded the data, and there is nothing to recover.

header-lost.why: The file's first cluster is lost, so it cannot be identified or opened as what it was.

half-or-more-lost.why: Half or more of the file's clusters are lost.

clusters-lost.why: Some of the file's clusters are lost - overwritten, or now allocated to a live file - and the rest survive.

damage-unlocated.why: The format's own checks fail (checksums, sample framing), but not at a location that says which clusters are lost.

unverified-after-break.why: The format's validator stopped at a break; the clusters after it could not be checked.

validated-prefix.why: The file is larger than the validation limit, so only its beginning was checked; that beginning holds up.

truncated.why: The content ends before its own structure does.

location-guessed.why: The filesystem kept only the first cluster; the rest of the layout is assumed contiguous.

location-unknown.why: Nothing records where the file's content was.

path-untrusted.why: The folder the file was in could not be established.

no-structural-check.why: No validator exists for this format, so the rating rests on metadata and content evidence alone: a cluster overwritten with bytes that look like the file's own would not be seen.

_uniform_doc: A cluster of one repeated byte is evidence of loss where the format cannot
contain one. Compressed image data never can. Zero-filled regions are
ordinary in databases, containers, uncompressed media and executables -
SQLite's secure_delete zeroes pages, MP4 pads with free boxes - so for
those only a non-zero, non-0xFF fill counts. Text may contain a run of a
printable character (fixed-width padding) but not of anything else. For a
format the rules do not know, 0x00 and 0xFF runs are treated as ordinary.
